title: Tertiary syphilis: vulvar gumma (with cardiovascular + neurosyphilis)
vignette: A 35-year-old woman comes to the office due to a vulvar lesion. She has also experienced occasional headaches and memory loss recently. The patient has had unprotected sexual intercourse with multiple partners. Cardiovascular examination is notable for a diastolic murmur with a prominent second heart sound. There is a painless indurated nodule on her vulva. Cervical cultures are negative for gonorrhea, but a serum Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) test is positive. Chest x-ray reveals calcifications at the level of the ascending aortic arch. Blood cultures are negative. Lumbar puncture shows mild pleocytosis and a positive VDRL result. HIV testing is negative. Which of the following best describes this patient's vulvar lesion?

clues.note: Headaches and memory loss with CSF pleocytosis and a positive CSF VDRL indicate NEUROSYPHILIS - a manifestation of late syphilis.

clues.text: diastolic murmur with a prominent second heart sound
clues.note: Aortic regurgitation (diastolic murmur) from a dilated aortic root is a feature of CARDIOVASCULAR (tertiary) syphilis.

clues.text: painless indurated nodule on her vulva
clues.note: In the setting of tertiary syphilis, a painless indurated granulomatous nodule is a GUMMA (not a primary chancre).

clues.text: calcifications at the level of the ascending aortic arch
clues.note: Ascending aortic calcification reflects syphilitic aortitis (vasa vasorum endarteritis) - cardiovascular tertiary syphilis, confirming late-stage disease.

whatMatters: This patient has TERTIARY syphilis: cardiovascular syphilis (aortitis -> aortic regurgitation + ascending aortic calcification) and neurosyphilis (headaches, memory loss, CSF pleocytosis, positive CSF VDRL). In this late stage, a painless indurated nodule is a GUMMA - a necrotizing granuloma. Answer E. (A chancre is PRIMARY syphilis; condyloma lata is SECONDARY.)
strategy: Stage the syphilis first: aortitis + neurosyphilis = TERTIARY. Then classify the lesion by stage: primary = painless chancre; secondary = condyloma lata (and diffuse rash); tertiary = GUMMA. The vulvar nodule in tertiary disease is a gumma. Reject chancre (primary), condyloma lata (secondary), condyloma acuminata (HPV warts), and granuloma inguinale (Klebsiella granulomatis, Donovan bodies).

eliminations.label: Chancre - PRIMARY syphilis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a painless, indurated ulcer at the inoculation site in PRIMARY syphilis (1-3 weeks after exposure). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has LATE (tertiary) syphilis (aortitis + neurosyphilis), where the lesion is a gumma, not a chancre. ✅ Correct if: an early painless genital ulcer (primary syphilis).

eliminations.label: Condylomata acuminata - HPV warts
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: anogenital warts caused by HPV (types 6/11). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are viral warts, unrelated to syphilis. ✅ Correct if: soft, cauliflower-like genital warts (HPV).

eliminations.label: Condylomata lata - SECONDARY syphilis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: broad, gray, wart-like, highly infectious lesions of SECONDARY syphilis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they appear in the secondary (bacteremic) stage with a diffuse rash; this patient is in the TERTIARY stage. ✅ Correct if: secondary syphilis with a maculopapular rash on palms/soles.

eliminations.label: Granuloma inguinale - Klebsiella granulomatis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a genital ulcerative disease caused by Klebsiella (Calymmatobacterium) granulomatis, with beefy-red ulcers and Donovan bodies. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a different STI, not a syphilitic gumma; VDRL/aortitis point to syphilis. ✅ Correct if: painless beefy-red ulcers with intracytoplasmic Donovan bodies.

reasoning: Aortitis (aortic regurgitation + ascending aortic calcification) + neurosyphilis (headache, memory loss, CSF pleocytosis, +CSF VDRL) = TERTIARY syphilis
In tertiary syphilis, painless indurated granulomatous nodules are gummas
The vulvar nodule is therefore a gumma
mechanism: Syphilis (Treponema pallidum) progresses through stages. PRIMARY: a painless, indurated CHANCRE at the inoculation site (1-3 weeks). SECONDARY (bacteremic, 5-10 weeks later): a diffuse maculopapular rash including palms/soles, plus CONDYLOMATA LATA (gray, wart-like, highly infectious). LATENT: asymptomatic. TERTIARY (years later): three classic manifestations - CARDIOVASCULAR syphilis (endarteritis of the vasa vasorum -> ascending aortic aneurysm/aortitis with calcification and aortic valve INSUFFICIENCY, giving a diastolic murmur), NEUROSYPHILIS (which can occur at any stage - here headaches/memory loss with CSF pleocytosis and positive CSF VDRL), and GUMMAS - painless, indurated GRANULOMATOUS lesions that progress to necrotic, white-gray ulcers on skin, mucosa, bone, or viscera. Given the cardiovascular and neurologic findings, this patient has tertiary syphilis, so her painless indurated vulvar nodule is a GUMMA (not the primary-stage chancre or the secondary-stage condyloma lata). Diagnosis uses nontreponemal (VDRL/RPR) plus treponemal tests; treatment is penicillin.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > syphilis stages: primary (chancre), secondary (rash + condyloma lata), tertiary (gummas, cardiovascular aortitis/aortic regurgitation, neurosyphilis); VDRL/RPR + treponemal tests; treat penicillin.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Cardiovascular + neurosyphilis = tertiary stage, so the painless nodule is a gumma.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on gumma, chancre, condyloma lata vs acuminata, syphilitic aortitis, or neurosyphilis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Chancre = primary; condyloma lata = secondary; condyloma acuminata = HPV; granuloma inguinale = Klebsiella (Donovan bodies).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: tertiary syphilis = gummas + cardiovascular (aortitis/aortic regurgitation) + neurosyphilis; VDRL positive; treat penicillin.
